hints: Write Newton's second law for $P$ moving up the smooth incline: $T - mg\sin\theta = ma$.
Write Newton's second law for $Q$ hanging vertically and descending: $m_Q g - T = m_Q a$.
Add the two equations to eliminate $T$ and solve for $a$.
Substitute $a$ back to find the tension $T$.
walkthrough:
State Newton's second law for particle $P$ ($m_P = 0.3\text{ kg}$) accelerating up the smooth slope of angle $\theta$ (where $\sin\theta = \frac{3}{5} = 0.6$):
$$T - m_P g\sin\theta = m_P a$$
$$T - 0.3 \times 10 \times 0.6 = 0.3a \implies T - 1.8 = 0.3a \quad \text{[Equation 1]}$$

State Newton's second law for hanging particle $Q$ ($m_Q = 0.2\text{ kg}$) accelerating downwards:
$$m_Q g - T = m_Q a$$
$$0.2 \times 10 - T = 0.2a \implies 2 - T = 0.2a \quad \text{[Equation 2]}$$

Add Equation 1 and Equation 2 to eliminate $T$:
$$(T - 1.8) + (2 - T) = 0.3a + 0.2a$$
$$0.2 = 0.5a$$
Divide by $0.5$:
$$a = \frac{0.2}{0.5} = 0.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Substitute $a = 0.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$ into Equation 2 to find $T$:
$$T = 2 - 0.2 \times 0.4 = 2 - 0.08 = 1.92\text{ N}$$

hints: Particle $Q$ accelerates downwards from rest through a distance of $0.8\text{ m}$.
Use $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ with $u = 0$ and $a = 0.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough:
State the kinematic formula for displacement under uniform acceleration from rest:
$$s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$$
Substitute $u = 0$, $s = 0.8\text{ m}$, and $a = 0.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$0.8 = 0 + \frac{1}{2} \times 0.4 \times t^2$$
$$0.8 = 0.2t^2$$

Divide both sides by $0.2$:
$$t^2 = \frac{0.8}{0.2} = 4$$
Taking the positive square root:
$$t = 2\text{ s}$$

hints: Find the velocity of $P$ at the moment $Q$ hits the floor: $v = at = 0.4(2) = 0.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
When the string goes slack, the only force along the plane on $P$ is the downhill component of gravity: $a = -g\sin\theta = -6\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Calculate the time for $P$ to return to the position where the string went slack: $t = 2 \times \frac{v}{|a|}$.
Add the initial $2\text{ s}$ to the slack duration to get the total elapsed time.
walkthrough:
Calculate the speed of particle $P$ at the moment $Q$ impacts the floor:
$$v = u + at = 0 + 0.4 \times 2 = 0.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Determine the acceleration of $P$ during the slack phase:
With tension gone, the only force acting parallel to the smooth incline is the downhill component of weight:
$$\Sigma F = ma \implies -mg\sin\theta = ma$$
$$a = -g\sin\theta = -10 \times 0.6 = -6\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Determine the time spent until the string becomes taut again:
Particle $P$ moves up the incline to instantaneous rest and then slides back down to the position where the string became slack.
Time to instantaneous rest at the top:
$$v_{\text{top}} = v + at_1 \implies 0 = 0.8 - 6t_1 \implies t_1 = \frac{0.8}{6} = \frac{2}{15}\text{ s}$$
By symmetry, sliding back down takes the same time $t_2 = \frac{2}{15}\text{ s}$.
Total slack time:
$$t_{\text{slack}} = t_1 + t_2 = \frac{2}{15} + \frac{2}{15} = \frac{4}{15}\text{ s} \approx 0.2667\text{ s}$$

Calculate the total time from release:
$$t_{\text{total}} = t_{\text{stage 1}} + t_{\text{slack}} = 2 + \frac{4}{15} = \frac{34}{15}\text{ s} \approx 2.27\text{ s}$$
